extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions obtained from crowd workers.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection was a two-step crowdsourcing process. First, crowd workers were presented with filtered candidate passages from science textbooks and asked to select a passage and formulate a question about it. Second, another worker generated three incorrect answer options (distractors) for the question, assisted by a model trained to predict plausible distractors.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The base corpus consists of 28 science study textbooks sourced from online learning platforms like CK-12 and OpenStax, covering subjects such as biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics from elementary to introductory college levels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-step crowdsourcing process where workers first select a passage from three options and generate a question and correct answer based on specific constraints (e.g., length limits, no yes/no questions, querying general principles). In the second step, another worker generates three incorrect answer options (distractors) with the help of model-generated suggestions. Workers were provided with examples of desirable and undesirable questions along with explanations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 workers per item (one for generating the question and correct answer, and a second for generating the distractors)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A machine learning model (random forest) trained on real science exam questions used to predict and suggest plausible answer distractors to assist human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split into training, validation, and test sets. It is intended to be used to investigate neural model performance in medium-sized data settings and to augment training data for answering real science exam questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to the base corpus to remove unsuitable sentences based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity rules.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The final filter included lexical, grammatical, pragmatical and complexity based rules. Specifically, sentences were filtered out if they i)were a question or exclamation ii)had no verb phrase iii)contained modal verbs iv)contained imperative phrases v) contained demonstrative pronouns vi)contained personal pronouns other than third-person vii)began with a pronoun viii) contained first names ix)had less than 6 or more than 18 tokens or more than 2 commas x)contained special characters other than punctuation xi)had more than three tokens beginning uppercase xii)mentioned a graph, table or web link xiii) began with a discourse marker (e.g. ‘Nonetheless’ )xiv)contained absoulute wording (e.g. ‘never’, ‘nothing’, ‘definitely’ )xv)contained instructional vocabulary ( ‘teacher’ ,‘worksheet’ , . . . ).
